background_notes.fact: A compact subset K of Euclidean ℝ^n is bounded and is contained in [-L,L]^n for some finite real L≥1, also for n=0.

grounds.reason: E lies in finite-dimensional Euclidean ℝ^n.
The Euclidean metric and the singleton convention in dimension zero are specified.

background_notes.justification: The open balls about the Euclidean origin of positive integer radius cover ℝ^n. A finite subcover of K gives a finite radius bound (the empty case is immediate). Each coordinate difference from the origin is bounded by the Euclidean distance; choosing L≥1 larger than the finitely many radii gives the box. In dimension zero the box is the singleton ambient space.

background_notes.fact: For n>0, L≥1 and 0<h0≤1, the box [-L,L]^n has a finite cover by closed coordinate cubes of side h0 with cardinality at most (2L/h0+2)^n≤(2L+2)^n h0^(-n). Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most √n h0, so for a>n its total a-cost is at most (2L+2)^n n^(a/2) h0^(a-n).

grounds.reason: F001 supplies the box containing E.
The witness L, branch n>0, conditions a>n and 0<h0≤1, and the coordinate-grid construction are explicitly supplied.
Distance is the square root of the sum of squared coordinate differences.

background_notes.justification: In each coordinate take k=ceil(2L/h0) successive closed intervals of length h0 starting at -L; they cover [-L,L] and k≤2L/h0+1≤2L/h0+2. Their n-fold products form the stated grid cover. Two points in a cube differ by at most h0 in each coordinate, giving squared distance ≤n h0². Summing the resulting diameter powers and using 2L/h0+2≤(2L+2)/h0 gives the displayed bound. This expands the stated grid estimate without changing its construction.

background_notes.fact: For fixed finite K>0, p>0 and t>0, one can choose 0<h≤t with K h^p<ε for each ε>0. Consequently a nonnegative scale-content infimum is zero if it admits such covers for every ε at that fixed scale.

grounds.reason: K=C n^(a/2)>0 is finite, p=a-n>0, and a mesh may be taken below min(1,δ0/√n)>0 because n>0 and δ0>0.
H^a_δ0 is the infimum of nonnegative cover costs and H^a is the supremum of those contents.

background_notes.justification: Positive real powers are increasing and obey (x^(1/p))^p=x for x>0. Choose 0<h<min(t,(ε/K)^(1/p)), so K h^p<ε. Every resulting grid is δ0-admissible, hence 0≤H^a_δ0(E)≤K h^p<ε. If this extended infimum were positive, a smaller positive finite ε would contradict the inequality; therefore it is zero. This holds separately for every δ0>0, whose supremum is thus zero; no limit is interchanged with a supremum.

background_notes.fact: For compact K⊆ℝ^n and finite δ>0, finitely many open balls of radius δ/2 centered in K cover K. Each has diameter at most δ, giving a finite total s-cost for every finite s>0.

grounds.reason: s>0 and δ>0 are fixed reals; the specified balls are centered at points of E.
Diameter is the supremum of pairwise Euclidean distances.
Finite covers are allowed countable covers, with empty members contributing zero.

background_notes.justification: Every center belongs to its positive-radius open ball, so these balls form an open cover. Compactness gives a finite subcover. For any two points of one ball, the triangle inequality bounds their distance by δ, hence its diameter is ≤δ. If there are k balls, their cost is ≤k δ^s<∞. Padding by empty sets if needed gives a countable admissible cover, whose finite cost bounds the defining infimum.
